chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Muhassin from Yunus ibn Ya'qub who said:

I sent to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and said to him: 'Doves were taken out of it from Medina to Mecca, then it was taken out from Mecca to Kufa.' He said to him, 'I think they were fresh (not yet fully fattened/ready). Tell him to slaughter a sheep for every bird.'

And whoever closes his door on a bird and it dies, if he closed it while he was Muhrim (in Ihram state), then upon him is its value. And if he closed it after he had entered Ihram, then upon him is a sheep. And if it is from the birds of the Haram (sanctuary), then upon him is its value, which he spends to buy fodder for the birds of the Haram. Narrated.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.طُيُور الْحَرَم: The specific birds (often pigeons/doves) native to the sanctuary of Mecca
key_terms.فُرْهَة: Fresh or newly arrived (birds), indicating they were not yet fully fattened or ready for consumption
key_terms.قِيمَة: The monetary value or price of the item

ai.seo_question: What is the kaffarah (expiation) for a pilgrim who kills a bird?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific financial expiations (kaffarah) for a pilgrim who kills birds, distinguishing between intentional acts and accidental deaths caused by confinement. It highlights the scholarly nuance that while killing sanctuary birds typically requires paying their value for fodder, the ruling shifts to a sheep sacrifice if the bird is killed while the pilgrim is still in the state of Ihram, reflecting the heightened sanctity of the ritual state.
